runs.text: Qatar, judged like Israel. Ready? The test: the same apartheid definition used on Israel. About eighty eight percent of people living in Qatar are not citizens. Become a citizen? <<ˈ|l|ɪ|v>> there twenty five years. Then, no more than fifty people a year. Change jobs? For years, workers needed their employer's permission. Reforms came in twenty twenty. Vote? Non-citizens never could. In twenty twenty four, even citizens voted to end their elections. By the same definition used on Israel: is this apartheid? You decide. Israel: one in five citizens is Arab. They vote. Arab parties won nineteen seats. Arab judges sit on the Supreme Court. Qatar is rarely called apartheid. Israel is called it daily. Both have real problems. One standard. So, let's run the test again.
